texts.gazette-2504-09: ශ්‍රී ලංංකාා ප්‍රජාාතාාන්ත්‍රිකා සමාාජාවාාදී ජානරජායේ� ගැැසට් පත්‍රය අති වියේ�ෂ The Gazette of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka EXTRAORDINARY අංකා 2504/09 - 2026 සැප්තාැම්බර් මාස 01 වාැනි අඟහරුවාාදාා - 2026.09.01 No. 2504/09 - TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 01, 2026 (Published by Authority) PART IV (B) — LOCAL GOVERNMENT Notices under the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance FILLING OF A VACANCY IN THE OFFICE OF MEMBER OF THE PASBAGE KORALE PRADESHIYA SABHA UNDER SECTION 66A(1)(a) OF THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES ELECTIONS ORDINANCE (CHAPTER 262) WHEREAS the Office of a member of the Pasbage Korale Pradeshiya Sabha has fallen vacant by reason of Resignation; And whereas the Secretary of the Jathika Jana Balawegaya, the recognized political Party to which Mr. Dissanayaka Mudiyanselage Premarathna the member who belonged, was required by me under Section 66A(1)(a) of the aforesaid Ordinance, to nominate a candidate of that ward Number 08 Bawwagama of Pasbage Korale Pradeshiya Sabha who belongs to such party and is not disqualified under Section 9 of the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance (Chapter 262) and who shall be declared Elected as a member within a period of thirty (30) days; And whereas the Secretary of the aforesaid recognized political party has communicated the decision to nominate Mr. Kitnasamy Muralidharan to fill the such vacancy; Therefore I, Hewage Dhanushka Nalin Sampath Fernando, Returning Officer of the Pasbage Korale Pradeshiya Sabha, acting in terms of Section 66A(l)(a) of the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance (Chapter 262) do hereby declare that Mr. Kitnasamy Muralidharan was elected as the member of the ward Number 08 Bawwagama of the Pasbage Korale Pradeshiya Sabha. H. D. N. Sampath Fernando, Returning Officer, Pasbage Korale Pradeshiya Sabha. District Elections Office, Kandy, 01st September, 2026. Gardiner Mawatha, Colombo 02 and bearing Company Registered No. PV 326 (hereinafter referred to as the ‘ Employer’) of the one part and INTER COMPANY EMPLOYEES UNION, a trade union duly registered under the Trade Unions Ordinance and having its registered office at No.10, Council Lane, Dehiwala (hereinafter referred to as the Union), of the other part, witnesseth: WHEREAS the Union has shown to the satisfaction of the Employer that it represents a majority of the Operative Grade Employees employed by the Employer AND WHEREAS it is the desire of the Union and the Employer to enter into an Agreement, which would ensure the peaceful adjustment and settlement of all disputes, which may arise between the Employer and its Employees and/or the Union and the promotion of industrial peace, productivity, quality and attendance. NOW THEREFORE for and in consideration of the above premises and the mutual terms and conditions hereinafter set out, the Union and the Employer agree as follows: 1. title This Agreement shall be known and referred to as “THE SOUTH ASIA GATEWAY TERMINALS (PVT) LTD COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT 2025” 2. date of operation and duration This Collective Agreement shall be effective from the First day of April Two Thousand Twenty Five and may be terminated by either party with one (01) month’ s written notice to the other, provided however, that neither party shall give such notice prior to the Thirty First day of March Two Thousand Twenty Eight. Any notice of termination of this Agreement given by either party, prior to the Thirty First day of March Two Thousand Twenty Eight, shall not be regarded as valid notice and shall be of no avail. It is the intention of both Employer and the Union to renew the agreement on the first day of April Two Thousand Twenty Eight and therefore negotiations for same may commence by the first of January Two Thousand Twenty Eight. 3. persons covered and bound This Agreement shall cover and bind the Employer, the Union and all the Quay Gantry Crane Operators, Rubber Tired Gantry (RTG) Crane Operators, Controllers Deck/Wharf, Controllers Yard, Reach Stacker/Fork Lift Operators, Receival Delivery Officers, Assistant Receival Delivery Officers, Foremen Electrical/Mechanical/Cargo Care, Terminal Engineering Assistants Electrical/Mechanical, Cargo Care Officers, Stores Officers, Assistant Stores Officers only who are employed on permanent contracts of employment by the Employer at its work places in the port of Colombo and who are members of the Union. 4. declaration of principle (a) Both Employer and the Union accept the principle that the special consideration affecting the Employer is such that the wage and salary rates are a proper subject for collective bargaining between the Employer and the Union, and that the actions of other employers including Government Corporations and the Government of Sri Lanka in their capacity as employers of labour, regarding the amount and timing of wage increases are not automatically relevant in the context of the Employer except where otherwise provided by legislation. (b) In cases in which Government does provide by legislation for benefits including increases in wages, gratuity, bonus etc., the following shall apply - I ෙකාටස: (I) ෙඡදය – (cid:636) ලංකා (cid:541)ජාතා(cid:486)(cid:437)ක සමාජවා(cid:463) ජනරජෙ(cid:591) අ(cid:431) (cid:618)ෙශෂ ගැස(cid:376) ප(cid:436)ය – 2026.09.04 3A PART I: SEC. (I) – GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY OF THE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF SRI LANKA – 04.09.2026 (i) When such benefits are more favourable than the benefits stipulated, only the difference between such benefits provided by such legislation and the benefits stipulated herein, shall be added to the said benefits stipulated herein, (ii ) When such benefits are equal or less favourable to the benefits stipulated herein, they shall not be added to or compounded with the said benefits stipulated herein, (c) The stipulations contained in Paragraph (b) above are without prejudice to the principle contained in Paragraph (a) above. 5. rights and responsibilities of employer Selection, placement, distribution, transfer and promotion of personnel, laying down of working hours and working programmes, planning and control of Terminal operations, introduction of new machinery or improved operational methods, expansion of operation facilities, establishment of quality and operations standards, maintenance of efficiency, the consequence thereof, maintenance of discipline in the Terminal and for that purpose taking necessary disciplinary action against employees within the framework of the existing law, regulations and standing orders, are exclusively the rights and responsibilities of the Employer. Recruitment, selection and placement of employees will depend on Employer’s requirement, which will not be based purely on the machinery plan. However, the Management acknowledges that the Union may raise with the Employer any grievance or dispute in the opinion of the Union that may have occurred to any of its members. 6. general terms and conditions of employment The terms and conditions of this Agreement shall, as from the date hereof, and during the continuance in force of this Agreement be deemed to be included in all the contracts of employment between the Employer and the Employees covered and bound by this Agreement, whether such contract of employment be written or oral or whether employment was subsisting as at the date hereof or shall come into being at any time after the date hereof but during the continuance in force of this Agreement. Provided, that in the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any pre-existing terms and conditions or practices, the terms and conditions of this Agreement shall prevail. 7. variation of terms and conditions of employment or benefits (a) The Union and its members and the Employees covered and bound by this Agreement jointly and severally agree with the Employer that during the continuance in force of this Agreement, they shall not seek to vary or add to all or any of the practices, terms and conditions of employment presently applicable to any of the employees covered and bound by this agreement or all or any of the benefits presently enjoyed by any of the workers covered and bound by this Agreement, other than by mutual agreement in writing. (b) This Agreement shall be deemed to be a full and final settlement of all matters covered herein as well as all matters raised by the Union or incidental thereto and in respect of which negotiations took place between the parties before the conclusion of this Agreement. 8. wages (a) As from the First day of April 2025 the Employer will grant an increase in wages of 15% on the consolidated wage applicable to each employee as at March 2025 with a minimum increment value of Rs.5,000. The minimum basic salary will be increased to Rs.30,000/ from 1st April 2025. The said wage for April 2025 shall be a consolidated wage. (b) As from the First Day of April 2026, the Employer will grant an increase in wages of 12% on the consolidated wage applicable to each employee as at March 2026 with a minimum increment value of 4,000/-. Provided, however, any absence without pay imposed by way of a decision of the Employer either pending the conclusion of disciplinary inquiry or by way of punishment will not be considered when ascertaining the eligibility of the Employee for the bonus payment. Subject to the above, other existing conditions and practices governing the payment of bonus shall remain unchanged. (b) year end unutilised leave bonus During any calendar year any employee who has an un-availed leave balance of 14 or more days of sick and casual leave, such employee will be granted a bonus equivalent to half a month’ s basic salary in the month of January in each year. However, any employee who has been placed on no pay leave even for half a day shall not qualify for this bonus payment. Provided, however, any absence without pay imposed by way of a decision of the Employer either pending the conclusion of disciplinary inquiry or by way of punishment will not be considered when ascertaining the eligibility of the Employee for the bonus payment. (c) leave encashment Employees will be paid for their unutilised sick/casual and annual leave as per the current practice. (d) attendance incentive (i) The Employer will pay a monthly attendance incentive to the Employees subject to the conditions set out herein. (ii) This incentive will be calculated monthly and paid once a month, based on the following criteria. a) An employee who reports for all rostered shifts in a calendar month will be paid Rs.10,000/-. b) An employee who avails half (½) a day’s or one ( l ) day’s leave during a calendar month will be paid Rs.7,000/-. c) An employee who avails one and half (1½) or two day’s (2) leave during a calendar month will be paid Rs.5,000/-. (ii) Unauthorised absence or any form of no-pay leave for any period of time will result in the loss of the total incentive for that month. (iv) Annual leave will, for this purpose, be reckoned as days present. (v) Employees will not be eligible for this incentive once they have exhausted their Sick/Casual Leave quota of that calendar year. However, any justifiable reason such as prolonged illness/accidents may be considered an exception, at the discretion of the Employer. (e) travelling allowance The Employer shall pay employees engaged in shift duties a daily transport allowance of Rs. 1,200/- as per the existing practice for each shift attended. (f) productivity based incentive scheme (PBIS) It is agreed by the Employer and the Unions that the Productivity Based Incentive Scheme ( PBIS) shall be as per the scheme set out in Schedule 2 hereto. 6A I ෙකාටස: (I) ෙඡදය – (cid:636) ලංකා (cid:541)ජාතා(cid:486)(cid:437)ක සමාජවා(cid:463) ජනරජෙ(cid:591) අ(cid:431) (cid:618)ෙශෂ ගැස(cid:376) ප(cid:436)ය – 2026.09.04 PART I: SEC. (i) government action on bonus If at any time during the continuance in force of this Agreement, the Government introduces by legislation for any scheme of bonus or payment under any attendance incentive or production scheme, the employees covered will not be entitled to the benefits of such scheme in addition to the bonus or bonuses provided for in this Agreement. (j) work during april new year holiday period With effect from April 2025 employees who engage in work in all rostered shifts/days during April New Year Holiday period from 12th day of April to 16th day of April each year will be granted a payment per working shift following the current practice. i. 2025 April - Rs.4,000/- ii. 2026 April - Rs.4,500/- iii. 2027 April - Rs.4,500/- 12. distress loan Confirmed employees who have a period of less than five-years of service in the permanent employment may apply for a distress loan amounting Rs.100,000/- once a year ( 12 months) and employees who have completed five years of service or more in the permanent employment may apply for a distress loan amounting Rs.200,000/- once a year (12 months) for an emergency requirement acceptable to the Employer. The recovery period of such loan will be twelve (12) months commencing from the date of granting the loan and the loan will be granted subject to the requirement of total deductions including the loan instalment not exceeding 60% of the salary of each month. 13. death mutual benefit scheme The Employer shall grant a sum of Rs.250,000/- to an Employee in the event of a death of his/her immediate family member ( namely the spouse, children and parents of the employee) and in the event of a death of his/her father-in-law or mother-in-law as defined in the existing Death Mutual Benefit Scheme. The total employee contribution for such event shall be Rs.150,000/- regulated in terms of Death Mutual Benefit Scheme. 14. employees insurance scheme Employees will be covered with the following insurance schemes. (a) Surgical and Hospitalisation Insurance Cover will be revised for the next 3 years as follows: Indoor - Rs.400,000/- per annum. Outdoor - Rs.60,000/- per annum. (b) The employer shall, on the written request of an employee, deduct from the wages due to such employee the current monthly union dues as are specified by the employee to be payable monthly by employees to the union and remit the amount so deducted to the union. (c) Every employee who agrees to the deduction of union dues from his wages shall sign an “authorisation” and forward it to the employer. (d) Every employee shall be entitled to withdraw his agreement to check off at any time by signing a statement to that effect and forwarding it to the Employer. 16. employees’ grievances procedure In the event of an employee grievance, the following procedure shall be followed in resolving such grievance. (a) The Employee will, in the first instance discuss the grievance with the Departmental Executive. (b) If the grievance is not satisfactorily resolved, the employee may then discuss the matter with the Departmental Manager. The Departmental Manager will if necessary, in consultation with the Employer’ s Management endeavour to arrive at a satisfactory solution in respect of the grievance. (c) In the event of the grievance not being resolved at the level of the Departmental Manager, the issue in Grievance will then be discussed by the Employee with the Employment Practices Manager/Human Resource Manager of the Employer. (d) If no satisfactory solution is arrived at, then the issue in grievance will be discussed by the Branch Union and the Employer ‘s Management. At such discussion, the number of representatives from each side shall not exceed four (4) . 17. disputes resolution procedure In the event of a dispute pertaining to a matter not covered by this Agreement, both parties agree that they shall settle such dispute by strictly adhering to the procedure set out below: a) Whenever, there is a dispute, a written statement of the dispute shall be forwarded by the branch union to the Employer, and at least two weeks ‘ time given for the employer to resolve the dispute. b) If no satisfactory solution is found, the matter shall be referred to the parent union and to the Employers ‘ Federation of Ceylon ( EFC) for the purpose of attempting to resolve the dispute. 8A I ෙකාටස: (I) ෙඡදය – (cid:636) ලංකා (cid:541)ජාතා(cid:486)(cid:437)ක සමාජවා(cid:463) ජනරජෙ(cid:591) අ(cid:431) (cid:618)ෙශෂ ගැස(cid:376) ප(cid:436)ය – 2026.09.04 PART I: SEC. Employee benefits as per the Collective Agreement will remain unchanged provided Employees continue with the agreed work practices, terms and condition stipulated in this agreement. 21. breaches of the agreement by the union and / or its members If in the opinion of the Employers ‘Federation of Ceylon, the Union or their members have committed a breach of this Agreement, then and in such event the Employer reserves the right, inter alia, to withdraw all or any of the facilities or benefits granted to the Employees, or to the Union seven ( 7) days’ after raising such breach with the Union in writing without prejudice to the Employer’s right to restore such facilities or benefits upon such terms and conditions as the Employer and the Employers, Federation of Ceylon may decide. The Union will be entitled to dispute the justification of such withdrawal. If in the opinion of the Union, the Employer has committed a breach of this Agreement then and in such event, the Union would have the right to refer such matter to the Commissioner of Labour. 22. interpretation of agreement Any dispute over the interpretation of this Agreement shall be settled by voluntary arbitration under section 3 (i) (d) of the Industrial Dispute Act ( 1950) . 23. definitions Unless the context otherwise requires the following words shall have the following meaning- (a) “Employee” or “Workman” shall mean an employee in the permanent employment of the Company and is covered and bound by this Agreement . (b) “Dispute” shall have the same meaning as an “Industrial Dispute” in the Industrial Disputes Act ( 1950) as amended or in any Act enacted by the Parliament to replace the Industrial Disputes Act subject to the proviso that it shall not include a dispute involving a variation of this Collective Agreement . In the circumstances, I wish to quote majority decision of the Supreme Court in State Bank in India vs. Edirisinghe (1991) that the arbitrator has to make an award which is just and equitable, he is not tied down and fettered by the terms of the contract of employment. He can create new rights and introduce new obligations between the parties. The eff ect of the award is to introduce terms which become implied terms of the contract. It was pointed out that as industrial arbitrator creates a new contract for the future in contrasts to a judge who enforces rights and liabilities arising out an existing contract. An industrial arbitrator settles disputes by dictating new conditions of employment to come into force in the future when he cannot get the parties to agree to them in contrast to a judge who determines the existing right and liabilities of the parties. In the circumstances taking into consideration the totality of evidence led before me I make no award. Kapila M. (1) These rules shall apply to any person who directly or indirectly contravenes any provision of the Act or any rule, direction or decision made or issued thereunder. (2) These rules shall not apply to any employee of the Central Bank who is governed by the provisions of any rule, direction or decision made or issued under the Act relating to disciplinary control of such employees. 3. Where any Head of Department of the Central Bank (hereinafter referred to as the “Head of Department”) has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has directly or indirectly contravened any provision of the Act, or any rule, direction or decision made or issued thereunder, such Head of Department shall, as soon as practicable, cause an examination, investigation or inquiry, as the case may be, to be conducted into such matter. 4. (1) Where, pursuant to the examination, investigation or inquiry conducted under rule 3, any direct or indirect contravention of any provision of the Act, or any rule, direction or decision made or issued thereunder, is prima facie identified, the Head of Department shall issue a notice in writing to the person who is alleged to have committed such contravention, informing such person of such contravention, and requiring such person to show cause, within such period as specified in such notice, as to why such person shall not be held to have committed such contravention. (2) (a) The notice shall set out - (i) the findings of the examination, investigation or inquiry, as the case may be, pertaining to the alleged contravention; and (ii) the time period within which such person is required to show cause, which shall not be less than fourteen days from the date of the notice. (b) Such notice may, inter alia, require such person to provide information on, or respond to, any specific question raised therein relating to the alleged contravention. (3) Upon receipt of the notice, such person shall respond to such notice within the period specified therein, providing all material facts or information to substantiate as to why such person shall not be held to have committed such contravention. (4) Any extension of the time specified in the notice shall not be granted to such person to respond to the notice, unless the Head of Department is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds to do so. (5) Any person who fails to respond to the notice issued under this rule shall be deemed to have accepted the liability of the contravention specified therein. 5. (1) The Head of Department shall, without undue delay, consider the response received by him pursuant to sub-rule (3) of rule 4. In considering such response, he shall take the following factors into account: - (a) the severity of the alleged contravention and whether such contravention is recurring; (b) whether any loss or damage is caused to the depositors or any other person due to such contravention; (c) whether the person alleged to have committed such contravention is unduly benefitted from such contravention; (d) the financial resources of the person alleged to have committed the contravention; (e) any mitigating factors; and (f) such other matter as the Head of Department considers to be relevant. (2) The following factors may be considered when issuing a letter of reprimanding or severe reprimanding: - (a) the severity or recurrence or continuation of the contravention; (b) the position held by the person who committed such contravention; (c) the systemic importance of the financial institution, where applicable; and (d) any other relevant factor as may be considered to be relevant by the Committee or the Governing Board, as the case may be, based on the circumstances pertaining to each such matter. 12. (1) An administrative fine referred to in rules 6 and 7 shall be- (a) in the case of an administrative fine imposed by the Committee under rule 6, an amount not exceeding Rupees five million; (b) in the case of an administrative fine imposed by the Governing Board under rule 7, an amount not exceeding two-thirds of the maximum fine specified in section 111 of the Act. (2) The Central Bank may, if it considers such publication necessary, publish the information relating to administrative fines imposed by the Committee or the Governing Board under these rules in such form and manner as may be decided by the Central Bank. (3) All administrative fines shall be payable to the special account maintained for the purpose at the Finance Department of the Central Bank. 13. (2) Where the person who is found to have committed the contravention is the Chairman of the Board of Directors of a financial institution, a copy of the communication referred to in rule 8 shall also be sent to the Secretary to the Board of Directors of such financial institution, directing such Secretary to place such communication before the Board of Directors at the meeting which will be held immediately after the date of receipt of such communication. 14. (1) A person aggrieved by any administrative measure taken by the Committee under rule 6 shall be entitled to make an appeal to the Governing Board, within a period of fourteen days from the date of receipt of the communication referred to in rule 8. The Chairperson shall appoint an officer of the Central Bank not below the rank of a Deputy Director as the Secretary to the Committee. 17. (IIA) - GAZETTE OF THE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF SRI LANKA -04.06.2026 Notice HOMOEOPATHIC MEDICAL COUNCIL Recruitment to the Post of Homoeopathic Medical Officer at the Homoeopathic Medical Council APPLICATIONS are invited from Sri Lankan citizens who possess the following qualifications for recruitment to the post of Homoeopathic Medical Officer for new government Homoeopathic medical clinics to be established by the Homoeopathic Medical Council. 01. Post :- Homoeopathic Medical Officer 02. Nature of Appointment :- Permanent. Entitled to Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) benefits. 03. Salary Scale :- Service Category Code and Monthly Salary Scale (MM 1-1-2016: Rs. (53,175 - 10×1,375 - 15×1,910 - 95,575/-) 04. Required Qualifications :- Possession of a degree in Homoeopathic Medicine obtained after completing a degree course of not less than five and a half (5½) years duration at a local or foreign university recognized by the University Grants Commission of Sri Lanka. Or Completion of a full-time diploma course of not less than four (04) years in Homoeopathic Medicine from a university recognized by the University Grants Commission of Sri Lanka, along with three (03) years of professional experience thereafter. And Completion of at least one (01) year of internship training and registration as a Homoeopathic Physician in the Homoeopathic Medical Council. Possession of at least one (01) year of professional experience (in medical clinical practice) at a local or foreign hospital, institution, or clinic. (This must be proven by a patient register of those treated along with the official seal of the head of the institution confirming service at the said institution, or if it is a privately run institution, it must be confirmed by a certificate from the Divisional Secretary of the relevant area where the institution was operated. 05. Age Limit :- Should be not less than 25 years and not more than 50 years of age. 06. Other :- Every applicant, I. Must be a citizen of Sri Lanka. II. Must possess the physical and mental fitness required to properly perform the duties assigned to the post as well as to serve in any part of the island. III. Must possess an excellent character. 07. Recruitment Procedure :- Recruitment will be made in order of merit based on the results of a structured interview conducted by a board appointed by the appointing authority. 08. (IIA) - GAZETTE OF THE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF SRI LANKA - 11.09.2026 MINISTRY OF EDUCATION, HIGHER EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL EDUCATION Efficiency Bar Examination III for Pirivena Teachers, Approved Appointment-Holding Teachers in Government-Approved Private Schools, and Approved Appointment-Holding Teachers in Assisted Special Schools - 2026 IT is hereby notified that the Department of Examinations, Sri Lanka, will conduct the Efficiency Bar Examination III in December 2026 and this examination is conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Third Amendment to the Sri Lanka Teacher Service Minute, published in the Extraordinary Gazette Notification of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka No. 2444/21 dated 08.07.2025, and the Fourth Amendment to the Sri Lanka Teacher Service Minute, published in the Extraordinary Gazette Notification of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka No. 2493/61 dated 19.06.2026 and it is also hereby notified that opportunities are provided for Pirivena Teachers, approved appointment-holding teachers in government-approved private schools, and approved appointment-holding teachers in assisted special schools to sit for this examination.This examination will be held only at the examination centers established in the cities specified in Schedule I, and subsequent changes to the requested city/cities will not be permitted. If an insufficient number of candidates apply for a particular city to establish an examination center, those candidates will be redirected to an examination center established in the city indicated as their second preference or another adjacent city. Further, if an insufficient number of candidates apply across all or most of the proposed cities, the Commissioner General of Examinations will make arrangements to conduct the examination in Colombo only. Applications are available on the website of the Department of Examinations, Sri Lanka (www.doenets.lk) under "Our Services" via "Online Applications - Recruitment/E.B. Exams". Applications can be submitted via the Online method only. The acceptance of online applications will be started on September 14 th , 2026, at 09:00 AM and closed on September 30 th ,2026, at 09:00 PM. Once the application is submitted online, it must be downloaded, and two (02) printed copies thereof must be obtained. The relevant sections on both copies must be completed in handwriting, the applicant's signature must be attested, and one copy, along with the certification of the Zonal Director of Education, must be included in the applicant's personal file. The other copy must be retained in the custody of the applicant to be presented whenever required. The applicant must bear any adverse consequences resulting from delaying the submission of applications until the closing date. 2.0 I. Candidates are subject to the rules and regulations prescribed by the Commissioner General of Examinations regarding the conduct of this examination. II. The rules enacted for obtaining candidature are printed separately in the Gazette . If these rules are violated, candidates will be subject to any punishment imposed by the Commissioner General of Examinations. III. Only Officers specified under Section 12.0 of the aforementioned services are eligible to apply for this examination. IV. If applicants with special needs are appearing for this examination, it must be mandatorily stated in the application form, and copies of the relevant medical certificates must be submitted to the Department of Examinations, Sri Lanka, along with a printed copy of the application. 3.0 EXAMINATION FEES: Since this Efficiency Bar Examination is being conducted for the first time, no examination fee shall be charged. 4.0 SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS: The online examination application must be completed in the English language only. The department will notify the applicant via SMS to the mobile phone number used to access the system, or via E-mail, whether the soft copy submitted online has been accepted/ or rejected, as a valid application. Download the instruction sheet prepared for applying for examinations before completing the online application. Follow those instructions accurately when filling out the application. No amendment made to the application after obtaining a printed copy will be considered as a valid amendment. Incomplete applications will be rejected without any notification. 5.0 Candidates must prove their identity inside the examination hall for every subject they appear for to the satisfaction of the Supervisor. When an inquiring is made, it will be useful to keep a photocopy of the completed application form to verify any information requested by the Department of Examinations. The admission card must be checked, and if there are amendments, the Department of Examinations must be contacted well in advance to make the relevant corrections according to the application. Requests for amendments made at the examination hall will not be considered. 7.0 The issuance of an examination admission card to a candidate shall not be considered an acceptance that he or she is eligible to sit for the exam or has completed the relevant Efficiency Bar requirement. 8.0 The applicant's signature on the examination admission card must be attested by the Zonal Director of Education or an Officer authorized by him. (a) The closing date for application is 30/10/2026 1. Functions assigned to the post: - Providing legal consultations to the District Offices, Agrarian Development Centres fallen under the Department of Agrarian Development and its scope, preparing legal documents such as draft bills, regulations, observation reports, proxies etc . - Maintaining coordination with the Department of Attorney General, taking action on complaints on human rights violations, and providing consultation regarding the court cases, of which the officers Department of Agrarian Development and in above mentioned public institutions fallen under the scope of the Department are named as respondents on matters relevant to the scope, and appearing before the court on such cases. - Providing consultations to take action as per Section 4,5,6 of the Chapter XXXIII and Section I of Chapter XI of the Establishments Code, providing necessary guidance, and carrying out other relevant activities and performing other duties entrusted by the Commissioner General of Agrarian Development. 2. Method of Recruitment: Out of the candidates, who have satisfied qualifications stipulated in the notification, the candidates who secure highest marks on the results of an interview to be held to evaluate the eligibility by an interview board appointed by the Public Services Commission will be recruited to the post fallen vacant. The interview will be held conforming to the marking scheme (Mentioned under No. 7) approved by the Public Services Commission. Active date of the appointment will be determined by Public Services Commission. 3314 I fldgi (II w ) fPoh ‑ YS% ,xld m%cd;dka;s%l iudcjd§ ckrcfha .eiÜ m;%h ‑ 2026'09'25 : P ART I : S EC . (The period of experience, official stamp of the attestor and the date of attestation should be clearly indicated in the documents submitted to prove the active and professional experience.) Or Should have possessed experience of not less than 03 years in a legal post* in a public institution after taking oath as an attorney at law at the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka. I. Coordination with the Department of Attorney general on court cases and carrying out legal affairs. II. Legal affairs connecting to agreements. III. Legal affairs on relevant acts and ordinances IV. Formulation of legal documents such as draft bills, circulars, regulations etc. V. Laws imposed by various Statutory Institutions, court cases or investigations. Note: The copies of the documents certified by the candidate him/herself, which prove the basic qualification of the candidate, should be attached to the application. Physical Fitness: Every candidate should be with sound physical and mental condition to perform the duties of the post and to serve at any part of Sri Lanka. 3.4. Other qualifications: (i.) The candidate should be with an excellent character. (ii.) The candidates, who are Government officers, should have not been subjected to any disciplinary punishment as per provisions in Public Services Commission Circular No. 01/2020. (iii.) Should have satisfied each and every way the qualifications prescribed for recruitment to the post as at the closing date of applications 30/10/2026. 4. Conditions for engagement in service: (i.) This post is permanent and pensionable. You are subjected to the policy decision taken in due course by the Government on the pension scheme to which you are entitled. Further you are required to contribute to Widows and Orphan's pension scheme/ Widower's and Orphan's Pension scheme and required to pay contributions as determined by Government from time to time. (ii.) This post is subjected to a probationary period of 03 years. It is required to pass the first efficiency bar examination as prescribed in the scheme of recruitment within 03 years from the date of recruitment to the post. (iii.) Should have acquired the competency in other official language/s as per the provisions stipulated in Public Administration Circular 18/2020 dated 16.10.2020. (iv.) This appointment is subjected to the procedural rules of the Public Services Commission, Establishments Code and Financial Regulations of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, scheme of recruitment for the post of Legal Officer in Grade III of Executive service category of the Department of Agrarian Development and conditions in the revisions already made or to be made in due course to the same. (v.) The candidate will not be allowed at later occasions to change the language medium applied by the candidate. The language medium, under which you are qualified to receive an appointment, will be the language medium you have indicated in your application.
